questions.question: Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cone with radius r, slant height l =
questions.explanation: CSA of cone = πrl (the lateral curved surface only). TSA = CSA + base = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r). Volume = (1/3)πr²h. Note: slant height l² = h² + r² (Pythagoras).

questions.explanation: l² = h² + r² = 576 + 49 = 625. l = 25 cm. (Pythagoras: the slant height is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs h and r.)

A solid cone (r = 14 cm, h = 48 cm) is melted and recast as a cylinder of same radius (r = 14 cm). Height of cylinder (π = 22/7):
questions.explanation: Volume cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π×196×48 = π×196×16. Volume cylinder = πr²H = π×196×H. Equating: 196×16 = 196×H → H = 16 cm.

questions.question: A cone and a cylinder have equal base radius and height. Ratio of their volumes =
questions.explanation: V_cone = (1/3)πr²h. V_cylinder = πr²h. Ratio = (1/3)πr²h : πr²h = 1 : 3. A cone always has 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height. This is a fundamental mensuration fact.

questions.question: A heap of grain is in the shape of a cone (r = 2.1 m, h = 2.8 m). Volume (π = 22/7) =
If the radius of a cone is doubled (height unchanged), volume becomes:
questions.explanation: V = (1/3)πr²h. New r = 2r. New V = (1/3)π(2r)²h = (1/3)π4r²h = 4V. Volume becomes 4 times. (Same as cylinder — volume scales as r².)

questions.question: A cone-shaped funnel: r = 14 cm, l = 50 cm. TSA (π = 22/7) =
Summary check: Formula for Volume of cone vs cylinder vs cuboid with same dimensions (r=7, h=14, l=b=7)?
options: Cone=718 cm³, Cylinder=2,156 cm³, Cuboid=686 cm³ — cone=(1/3)×cylinder; all differ
questions.explanation: V_cylinder = πr²h = (22/7)×49×14 = 2,156 cm³. V_cone = (1/3)×2,156 ≈ 718.67 cm³. V_cuboid = 7×7×14 = 686 cm³. So cylinder > cone > cuboid (roughly). Cone = 1/3 of cylinder with same base and height — always.
